title: Entitlement slices and proportional billing for shared accounts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: PRD for introducing per-subteam 'entitlement slices' within a single paid account and billing customers proportionally for consumption that exceeds individual slices. This enables enterprise customers to allocate quotas per org/team, apply soft overages at the slice level, and reconcile invoices to the account-level committed entitlements.
problem_statement: Large customers managing multiple product teams under a single Redwood account have requested fine-grained quota controls (per-team), predictable cost allocation, and a transparent overage policy that can be reconciled on invoices. Current plan entitlements are single numeric quotas per account which complicates internal chargebacks, causes sudden application throttles during cross-team bursts, and makes billing disputes common.
goals: Allow account admins to create named entitlement slices (sub-quotas) with configurable token quotas and soft overage rules
Meter consumption at both slice and account level and ensure invoice line items clearly show slice-level usage and proportional overage charges
Provide API and Console UX for slice management and visibility, including audit logs and alerts
Ensure backward compatibility: existing single-quota customers see identical billing unless they opt into slices
Ship acceptance criteria and end-to-end billing reconciliation tests before release
scope_included: Slice creation/deletion via Console and API
Per-slice adjustable token quotas and per-route rate limits
Soft overage window with configurable grace (minutes/hours) at slice level
Billing ledger changes to record slice-level usage and produce invoice line items for proportional overage
Migration CLI/API to split an account-wide entitlement into slices (admin-triggered)
Observability: slice-level usage dashboards, alerts for 80/90/100% consumption
scope_excluded: Automated chargeback payments between internal orgs (out of scope for MVP)
Per-user billing statements (only account invoices will show slice lines)
Complex multi-currency proportional allocation (MVP supports account currency only)
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Account admin can create up to 50 slices with name, quota (tokens), and soft overage config via Console and API
AC-2: Requests include a slice identifier; when provided, usage is recorded against slice and account. When absent, usage defaults to 'Unallocated' slice
AC-3: Soft overage triggers when slice consumption >= quota and lasts for configured grace window; consumption continues (subject to per-route rate limits) and overage tokens are flagged for billing
AC-4: Invoice shows a breakdown: base plan (committed tokens), slice allocations, slice usage, and any proportional overage charges with calculation detail
AC-5: Billing reconciliation tests (automated) validate invoiced overage equals computed overage within 0.1% tolerance across 10K+ events
AC-6: Rollout includes an opt-in toggle; existing accounts remain unchanged until admin enables slices
AC-7: Observability: dashboards expose slice-level P50/P95 latency, tokens consumed per hour, and alerts for 80/90/100% thresholds
AC-8: Permissions: only account admins and slice owners can modify slice configs; audit log entries created for all changes
AC-9: API contract documented and SDK examples added for Node/Python; backwards-compatible endpoints remain supported
rate_limit_rules: Per-route rate limits continue to be enforced at runtime; slices may carry a per-slice steady-state rate cap (tokens/sec)
When multiple slices share backend capacity, smart routing may apply additive or priority-based throttling to preserve account-level SLOs
Default behavior for no-slice requests: route to 'Unallocated' slice and use account-level quota
Burst allowances honored by slice when enabled; bursts are charged to overage if they exceed slice quota and grace window
quota_allocation_model: Named slices each receive a fixed token allotment billed as part of the account plan. Overage is computed first at slice granularity and then aggregated to the account invoice. The system supports percentage-based split in a follow-up release but MVP uses absolute token counts.
overage_policy: Soft overage: configurable grace window (0, 5m, 1h, 24h). During grace, requests are allowed and tokens counted as overage but not billed until window expires unless account-level enforcement is configured
Hard overage: if account-level emergency cap is hit (admin-configurable), further requests are rejected with 429
Overage rate: default per-token overage price is defined by customer plan; per-slice negotiated rates supported via contract metadata
Dispute window: customers can open a billing dispute within 60 days; meter logs and reconciliation data must be retained for 120 days
billing_reconciliation_steps: 1) Produce nightly ledger entries that aggregate slice-level usage into account-level invoice line items
2) Run reconciliation job that validates ledger totals equal runtime metering totals; discrepancies >0.1% flag a billing review ticket
3) Generate invoice CSV with columns: slice_id, slice_name, allocated_tokens, used_tokens, overage_tokens, overage_unit_price, overage_amount
4) Retain raw metering event IDs and aggregated rollups for 120 days for auditing
5) Add end-to-end test that simulates 3 slices, staggered consumption, and asserts invoice numbers match computed totals
ui_requirements: Console: Account > Entitlements page showing list of slices, allocated quota, used quota, remaining, and overage status
Slice detail view with edit modal, audit log, and quick 'increase/decrease allocation' controls for admins
Usage heatmap per slice (hourly) and alerts configuration panel
Migration wizard to split existing account quota into N slices with suggested allocations based on recent usage patterns
api_endpoints: Request header X-Redwood-Slice: <slice_id> or request.body.slice_id to attribute usage
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Internal): Feature gated behind org flag; integration tests + billing reconciliation smoke tests
Phase 1 (Pilot): Invite 5 enterprise customers for pilot; collect feedback and run reconciliation across live traffic
Phase 2 (General availability): Opt-in toggle in Console; marketing communication and updated T&Cs
Phase 3 (Migration): Provide CLI tool for large customers to split existing quotas with dry-run reports
Rollback: ability to disable slices for account and collapse usage back to account-level quota with full audit trail
monitoring_sla: Metering write latency must be < 200ms P99 for 95% of events
Reconciliation jobs succeed within 2 hours; failures create alert to billing-engineering on-call
Invoice generation window should complete within 4 hours nightly for accounts with slices
stakeholders: Engineering: Marcus Green (backend lead), Linh Tran (billing infra)
